# The command line

<!-- Generated by tools/make_command_line.py from the argument parser in src/mobcal/cli.py and the descriptions in src/mobcal/options.py. Edit those and run the tool; a test fails while this page differs from what it writes. -->

`mobcal` is the command line of MOBCAL, one command with a subcommand for each task. Everything the window does, the command line does too, by the same rules and with the same records ([The window](window.md)), and it also checks an installation and builds the programs from source. `mobcal` runs in any terminal once the installation folder is on the `PATH`, which the Windows installer offers to do, and in the **MOBCAL command prompt** of the Windows Start menu either way ([Installing MOBCAL](install.md)). The options of `mobcal run` and `mobcal import` that the window also sets carry the same descriptions as its tooltips, from one table in the package, so the two say the same thing about every setting they share. `mobcal COMMAND -h` prints the section of this page for that command.

- [`mobcal version`](#mobcal-version): Print the package version and the commit it was built from.
- [`mobcal self-check`](#mobcal-self-check): Check that this copy can compute a cross section.
- [`mobcal build`](#mobcal-build): Compile the helium and nitrogen programs with gfortran, from a source checkout.
- [`mobcal run`](#mobcal-run): Run calculations in parallel.
- [`mobcal clean`](#mobcal-clean): Remove the files the processes of finished divided runs left, as a run does itself when it succeeds.
- [`mobcal gui`](#mobcal-gui): Open the window.
- [`mobcal methods-text`](#mobcal-methods-text): Print the methods paragraph for runs.
- [`mobcal render-parameters`](#mobcal-render-parameters): Write the element table and the settings the program reads into a directory, for running the program there by hand.
- [`mobcal import`](#mobcal-import): Write an ion file from an ORCA output, a Gaussian output, or an .xyz file, with the charges you name, or from a .mfj, with its own.
- [`mobcal export`](#mobcal-export): Write the .mfj the 2012 program reads from an ion file.
- [`mobcal unpack`](#mobcal-unpack): Write the ion and method of a result file back as files, to run the calculation again.

## mobcal version

Print the package version and the commit it was built from.

```
usage: mobcal version [-h]
```

## mobcal self-check

Check that this copy can compute a cross section.

```
usage: mobcal self-check [-h] [--choline] [--report PATH]
```

- `--choline`: Also run the 2012 choline input in helium and compare it with the 2012 output, about 3 min.
- `--report PATH`: Write the report to this file as well.

## mobcal build

Compile the helium and nitrogen programs with gfortran, from a source checkout. An installed copy carries its programs and refuses this command.

```
usage: mobcal build [-h] [--gas {he,n2}] [--out DIR]
```

- `--gas {he,n2}`: One gas. Default: both.
- `--out DIR`: The output directory. Default: build/fortran/.

## mobcal run

Run calculations in parallel.

```
usage: mobcal run [-h] [--method KEY|PATH] [--seeds N[,N...]] [--rng {philox,ranlux}]
                  [--workers N] [--split W|auto] [--mode {in-order,balanced,throughput}]
                  [--dealing {static,claimed}] [--parameters PATH|NAME] [--out DIR]
                  [--skip-done] [--scratch {delete,zip,keep}]
                  [--result-ion {embed,reference}] [--temperature T] [--imp N] [--itn N]
                  [--inp N] [--inum N] [--inor N]
                  INPUT [INPUT ...]
```

- `INPUT`: The ions to run, one calculation for each input and seed. Paths to .mfj or .ion.json files, or globs.
- `--method KEY|PATH`: A preset of the gas, the element table, the random number generator, and the six run settings. The methods are 2012-he, the calculation of the 2012 release in helium, its element table and settings under RANLUX; 2012-n2, the same in nitrogen; 2012-philox-he, the 2012 helium table and settings under Philox4x32-10; 2012-philox-n2, the same in nitrogen; 2000-he, the calculation of the 2000 helium release, its table at 298 K and 25 trajectories per block under RANLUX; or the path of a method file. A table, generator, or setting given beside it overrides it, and the run records custom, or the shipped method the values make. Default: 2012-philox-he.
- `--seeds N[,N...]`: One run of each ion for every seed; the 2012 seed is 5013489. A method file may carry a seed of its own. A list of integers separated by commas, which wins over the seed of the method. Default: the seed of the method, 5013489 under a method without one.
- `--rng {philox,ranlux}`: The random number generator: Philox4x32-10, or RANLUX, the 2012 generator, which reproduces the 2012 outputs at the 2012 seed. Default: that of the method, philox under 2012-philox-he.
- `--workers N`: How many runs are in flight at once. Default: the number of cores divided by the processes per run, or under `--split` auto, the number it chooses.
- `--split W|auto`: How many processes each calculation is divided among. A divided run gives the serial result exactly. W processes, or auto, which chooses the runs in flight and the processes per run from the run count, the cores, and the ion sizes, in the mode chosen, dividing a run among at most 40 processes, no more than its slowest block of trajectories lets it use, and only when that saves at least 20 % of its time. Default: 1, one process per calculation.
- `--mode {in-order,balanced,throughput}`: How a batch of more runs than fit at once uses the cores. Finish in order runs one at a time, divided among every core it can use, so runs complete one after another and a pause waits for the run in flight. Balanced runs as many at once as keeps each divided run at least 70 % efficient (its time as one process, over the processes times its divided time): on a 40-core workstation, two choline runs at once in helium and one in nitrogen, and on 8 cores one at a time. Most throughput runs one process per run when there are at least as many runs as cores, which finishes the batch soonest and no run before the first wave ends. The counts are physical cores, not the logical processors hyperthreading doubles, which add a quarter to a third more throughput and make every run take about half as long again. in-order, balanced, or throughput; given alone, it implies `--split` auto, and beside `--split` W it is refused. Default: balanced.
- `--dealing {static,claimed}`: How a divided calculation shares its blocks of trajectories among its processes. Static gives each process a fixed share. Claimed lets each process take the next block no other has taken, so the processes finish together and one slowed by other work does not set how long the run takes. The result is the same either way. static or claimed. Default: claimed.
- `--parameters PATH|NAME`: The element table, which gives each atom of the ion its mass and its Lennard-Jones and hard-sphere parameters in the gas: a table the package ships, or a TOML file written for one gas. A path to a table for the gas of the method, or a shipped table by name: 2012 (He, N2), 2000 (He). Default: that of the method, 2012 under 2012-philox-he.
- `--out DIR`: The results folder of a study: each batch adds its run directories here, and summary.csv and summary.json are rewritten to cover every run it holds. Default: runs/.
- `--skip-done`: Leave out the runs the results folder already holds complete.
- `--scratch {delete,zip,keep}`: What a divided run that succeeds keeps of the files its processes wrote. Delete removes the folder of each process, the claim files, and the block files, after writing what only those folders held into the record.json of the run. Zip does the same but packs the block files into blocks.zip, which unpacked into the run directory lets the program redo the combining step there. Keep leaves every file. A run that fails or is stopped keeps every file whatever this says. delete, zip, or keep. Default: delete.
- `--result-ion {embed,reference}`: Whether the result file of each run, NAME.result.json, carries the geometries and charges of the ion or names the ion file by its name and SHA-256 alone, to keep result files small when the geometries are kept elsewhere. The method is in every result file either way. embed, which carries the ion, or reference. Default: embed.

### Run settings

The temperature and the five sampling counts the 2012 programs compiled in. Without these, every run uses the values of its method: the 2012 values (temperature 301 K, imp 1000, itn 10, inp 40, inum 250000, inor 30), or under 2000-he, 298 K and imp 25.

- `--temperature T`: The buffer gas temperature in kelvin, 301 K in 2012 and 298 K in 2000. It sets the velocity grid of the trajectory method and the conversion of each cross section to a mobility.
- `--imp N`: Trajectories per block of the trajectory method, one block for each velocity point in each cycle.
- `--itn N`: Cycles of the trajectory method, each an independent estimate of the collision integral, whose standard deviation the output reports.
- `--inp N`: Velocity points of the trajectory-method integration over the relative velocity.
- `--inum N`: Trajectories of the projection-approximation and exact hard-sphere pass, which the helium program alone makes.
- `--inor N`: The most reflections followed per trajectory of the exact hard-sphere pass.

## mobcal clean

Remove the files the processes of finished divided runs left, as a run does itself when it succeeds.

```
usage: mobcal clean [-h] [--scratch {delete,zip}] [--apply] DIR [DIR ...]
```

- `DIR`: Run directories, or folders of them.
- `--scratch {delete,zip}`: Delete the block files, or pack them into blocks.zip in each run directory. The folder of each process and the claim files go either way. Default: delete.
- `--apply`: Remove the files. Without it, the command lists what it would remove and removes nothing.

## mobcal gui

Open the window.

```
usage: mobcal gui [-h] [--check]
```

- `--check`: Open the window, close it, and exit 0: a test that it starts.

## mobcal methods-text

A methods paragraph for the completed runs, written from their records or result files: the program and version, method, gas, element table, temperature, trajectory counts, generator, and seeds, with the papers to cite; and the partial charges, when every run is of an ion file that carries its import record. Printed for the run directories, folders, and result files named.

```
usage: mobcal methods-text [-h] PATH [PATH ...]
```

- `PATH`: Run directories, folders of them, result files (NAME.result.json), or folders of result files.

## mobcal render-parameters

Write the element table and the settings the program reads into a directory, for running the program there by hand.

```
usage: mobcal render-parameters [-h] [--method KEY|PATH] [--parameters PATH|NAME]
                                GAS [DIR]
```

- `GAS`: The gas whose table is written: he or n2.
- `DIR`: Where to write parameters.tab and settings.tab. Default: the current directory.
- `--method KEY|PATH`: Write the table and settings of this method, a shipped method by its key or a method file by its path; it must be a method for the gas. Default: the default table for the gas and the 2012 settings.
- `--parameters PATH|NAME`: Write this TOML file, or this shipped table by name (2012 (He, N2), 2000 (He)), instead of the table of the method or the default table for the gas.

## mobcal import

Write an ion file from an ORCA output, a Gaussian output, or an .xyz file, with the charges you name, or from a .mfj, with its own.

```
usage: mobcal import [-h] [--charges KEY] [--net-charge Q] [--gas {he,n2,both}]
                     [-o OUT.ion.json] [--force]
                     SOURCE
```

- `SOURCE`: An ORCA output, a Gaussian output, an .xyz file, or a .mfj (the 2012 layout or the nine columns of MobCal-MPI).
- `--charges KEY`: Which atomic charges the imported ion carries: a set the file holds, such as CHELPG or Mulliken, or uniform, the net charge spread evenly over the atoms. The keys are mulliken, lowdin, chelpg, and hirshfeld for the blocks of an ORCA output; mulliken, hirshfeld, cm5, natural, mk, and chelpg for those of a Gaussian output; column for the fifth column of an .xyz file; and uniform. Without it, the import lists what the file holds.
- `--net-charge Q`: The net charge of the ion, in elementary charges. An .xyz file needs it; for an output it must agree with the charge the output was computed at.
- `--gas {he,n2,both}`: Whose element table the atoms must be in. Default: both.
- `-o OUT.ion.json, --out OUT.ion.json`: The ion file to write. Default: SOURCE-STEM_KEY.ion.json in the current directory, or SOURCE-STEM.ion.json for a .mfj.
- `--force`: Replace OUT.ion.json if it exists.

## mobcal export

Write the .mfj the 2012 program reads from an ion file.

```
usage: mobcal export [-h] [--gas {he,n2,both}] [--parameters PATH|NAME] [-o OUT.mfj]
                     [--force]
                     ION.ion.json
```

- `ION.ion.json`: The ion file.
- `--gas {he,n2,both}`: Whose element table gives each element its key; with both, each element must be in both tables. Default: both.
- `--parameters PATH|NAME`: This TOML file, or this shipped table by name (2012 (He, N2), 2000 (He)), instead of the default table for the gas.
- `-o OUT.mfj, --out OUT.mfj`: The file to write. Default: ION.mfj beside the ion file.
- `--force`: Replace OUT.mfj if it exists.

## mobcal unpack

The ion file and the method file of a calculation, written from its result file, which holds both, so that the calculation can be run again from the result file alone. Each file is checked against the SHA-256 the result file records, and the ion against the input the program read. A result file that names its ion by reference holds no ion to write and is refused. Writes NAME.ion.json and NAME.method.json, and prints the command that runs the calculation again.

```
usage: mobcal unpack [-h] [-o DIR] [--force] RESULT.result.json
```

- `RESULT.result.json`: The result file.
- `-o DIR, --out DIR`: The folder to write the two files into. Default: the current directory.
- `--force`: Replace a file of the same name that holds something else.
